note: Rolling grassland, woods and small lakes in Worth and Gentry counties, with an archery range. The map marks two camping spots on the gravel 213th Trail: this pin's lot at the west end beside a mown clearing between tree rows, and a second lot 0.9 km east by a mown clearing with a gravel lane. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: area page 'Camping: Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in designated areas', 14 days in 30; map (1/12/2026) marks two 'Camping site' symbols at lots on 213th Trail, GIS 110 (pin) and 142. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. PIN: GIS 110 is in a tree row 36 m N of its lot -> move to lot 971 40.41083,-94.25759. No split (both camps on 213th Trail, 0.86 km apart). Not waterfront kept. Phone: area page matches; brochure gives the Albany office.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Individual Campsites'. Brochure: 'Motor vehicles are restricted to graveled roadways and parking areas. Primitive camping is permitted only in designated areas and is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. 30 day maximum stay per year. Groups of 10 people or more must obtain a special use permit.' The map (Last Updated 1/12/2026) legend has 'Camping site'; two symbols, each beside a Parking symbol on 213th Trail. GIS camping points 110 and 142 (Type 'Primitive Camping Area'). Imagery: camp 110 = a ~25 x 20 m gravel lot on the north side of 213th Trail opening onto a mown clearing between tree rows; camp 142 = a gravel lot (979) on the south side of 213th Trail at a crossroads with a mown clearing behind it and a gravel lane south, two small campers parked on the grass in the leaf-on frame. Designated points beside gravel lots, so both stay. A 23-ft rig fits either lot. No ford/4WD/rig wording.
PIN: stored 40.41115,-94.25749 = GIS 110, which sits in a tree row 36 m north of its lot. Move to lot 971, 40.41083,-94.25759.

CLUSTERS / NO SPLIT: camp 142 at 40.41001,-94.24739 (lot 979 40.41023,-94.24702) is 0.86 km east on the same gravel 213th Trail - under 1 km and the same road. On imagery 142 is the more used of the two (campers on the grass, lane into the clearing); the pin's camp is also a mapped site, so the pin can stay on it.
WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept): no lake or stream within ~150 m of either camp; the area's small lakes are in the woods south and east.
PHONE: area page '(660) 626-1799' matches stored; the brochure's contact is the 'Albany Office ... (660) 726-3746'. Either is MDC's; stored left.
